title: Separation Processes
description: Separation Processes covers the principles and design methods used to separate chemical mixtures in industrial processes. Students apply phase equilibrium, mass transfer, staged-contact methods, and equipment design to distillation, absorption, stripping, extraction, leaching, membranes, adsorption, drying, and integrated process systems.

topics.title: Phase Equilibrium and Mass Transfer Foundations
topics.description: Students connect thermodynamics and transport to separations by learning how phase equilibrium and interphase mass transfer make separation possible.

children.title: Phase equilibrium
children.description: The point is to understand the thermodynamic limits that tell us whether a separation is feasible.

children.title: Raoult's law, Henry's law, and activity coefficients
Mass transfer
children.description: Students learn why separations take time and area rather than happening instantly at equilibrium.

children.title: Balances for separations
children.description: Material and energy balances anchor every separation design calculation.

topics.title: The Equilibrium-Stage Concept
topics.description: This module introduces idealized stages as the central design abstraction for distillation, absorption, extraction, and other staged operations.

children.title: Ideal stages
children.description: Stages let students represent contact between phases with a tractable design model.

children.title: Operating lines
children.description: Operating lines connect mass balances to graphical and algebraic design methods.

children.title: Stage-to-real equipment link
children.description: Students learn that ideal stages must be adjusted for real hardware.

topics.title: Flash Distillation
topics.description: Students learn the simplest vapor-liquid separation problem and use it to build intuition for equilibrium calculations and phase splits.

children.title: Flash calculations
children.description: Flash distillation teaches phase splits and equilibrium in the simplest useful separation setting.

children.title: Binary flash
children.description: Binary examples build intuition before moving to multicomponent systems.

children.title: Process uses
children.description: Students see where flash drums appear in plants.

topics.title: Multistage Distillation
topics.description: This topic develops staged distillation design for binary and multicomponent mixtures, including reflux, trays, and design tradeoffs.

children.title: Binary distillation design
children.description: Students learn how reflux and stages create sharper separations.

children.title: Tray and column operation
children.description: The gist is connecting graphical design to actual column behavior.

children.title: Multicomponent distillation
children.description: Students get a practical introduction to real mixture separations.

topics.title: Absorption and Stripping
topics.description: Students learn how gas-liquid contact is used to remove or recover solutes from process streams.

children.title: Gas-liquid contacting
children.description: Students learn how a liquid solvent removes a gas-phase solute or releases it during stripping.

children.title: Design methods
children.description: Design connects equilibrium, operating lines, and transfer units.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Examples show why absorption matters in environmental and process industries.

topics.title: Liquid-Liquid Extraction
topics.description: This module focuses on using a solvent phase to selectively separate components when distillation is impractical or inefficient.

children.title: Solvent selection
children.description: The point is to choose a solvent that improves separation without creating new problems.

children.title: Ternary phase behavior
children.description: Students learn to read phase diagrams used in extraction design.

children.title: Stage calculations
children.description: Extraction design applies staged-contact logic to liquid phases.

topics.title: Leaching and Solid-Liquid Extraction
topics.description: Students study how soluble material is removed from solids using solvent contact and mass-transfer principles.

children.title: Solid-liquid contact
children.description: Students learn how solute leaves a solid matrix and enters a solvent.

children.title: Leaching design
children.description: The design problem balances yield, solvent use, and contact time.

children.title: Industrial examples
children.description: Applications make the unit operation concrete.

topics.title: Membrane Separations
topics.description: This topic introduces pressure-, concentration-, and selectivity-driven separations using modern membrane systems.

children.title: Membrane transport
children.description: Students learn how selective barriers separate components.

children.title: Membrane processes
children.description: Different driving forces support different applications.

children.title: Module and system design
children.description: Membrane performance depends on module layout and fouling control.

topics.title: Adsorption and Ion Exchange
topics.description: Students learn how surfaces and solid media capture selected components for purification, recovery, or polishing.

children.title: Adsorption equilibrium
children.description: Students learn how solids take up solutes and how capacity is represented.

children.title: Fixed-bed operation
children.description: This subtopic connects adsorption behavior to column breakthrough.

children.title: Ion exchange
children.description: Students learn a related separation method driven by charge and resin selectivity.

topics.title: Drying and Humidification
topics.description: This module covers gas-vapor-solid operations where heat and mass transfer determine moisture removal and air-water behavior.

children.title: Psychrometrics
children.description: Students learn how air-water vapor mixtures are represented and used in humidification and drying.

children.title: Humidity, relative humidity, and wet-bulb temperature
Drying mechanisms
children.description: Drying design depends on heat and mass transfer from wet solids.

children.title: Equipment
children.description: Students connect drying theory to industrial hardware.

topics.title: Equipment Design and Sizing
topics.description: Students connect separation calculations to real equipment geometry, hydraulics, capacity, pressure drop, and operating limits.

children.title: Column internals
children.description: The point is to translate required stages or transfer units into real columns.

children.title: Capacity and hydraulics
children.description: Students learn operating constraints that can limit performance.

children.title: Design documentation
children.description: Separation designs need clear calculations and equipment specifications.

topics.title: Process Integration, Simulation, Safety, and Sustainability
topics.description: The course closes by placing separation units inside larger process systems, where economics, energy use, safety, and environmental impacts drive design choices.

children.title: Energy integration
children.description: Students learn why separations dominate plant energy use and how design can reduce utilities.

children.title: Simulation and optimization
children.description: Process simulators help evaluate realistic mixtures and design alternatives.

children.title: Safety and sustainability
children.description: Students connect separation choices to hazards and environmental impact.
